title: FSW01 14-round AES-256 Full-cipher algebraic representation

target.description: Full 14-round AES-256, including initial whitening and the standard final-noMC round. The reported description-size estimate uses normal-round branching throughout.

setting.key_relation: One AES master key with the standard key schedule. Public S-box affine constants are absorbed into dependent round-key offsets; repeated key bytes retain their dependencies.
setting.plaintext_model: Symbolic plaintext/ciphertext and dependent key variables; known pairs may instantiate equations, with no claimed efficient solver.
assumptions: Arithmetic is over GF(2^8) in the AES polynomial basis, with a/0=0, including at a=0.
S-box affine constants, byte positions and Frobenius powers are public. Absorbed round-key offsets remain dependent on the master key.
The source leaf-count model uses 32 summands per normal round and ignores the final-noMC simplification.
The Section 4 discussion of 2^26 key-byte appearances and 2^22 known pairs uses independent appearance variables. Actual AES key-byte occurrences remain dependent.

success.description: Probability and counts belong to the mathematical statement, not attack success or resource costs.

evidence.locator: PDF 1–9 / printed 103–111; PDF 2: zero convention and public offsets; PDF 3: Equation 1; PDF 4–5: Equations 4–5; PDF 6: Sections 2.2–2.3, reported counts; PDF 7–8: Section 4, conditional solver discussion.
evidence.interpretation: Complete primary reading and bounded forward checks. The nested representation retains zero branches and the dependencies of expanded key bytes.

limitations: The leaf counts estimate description size using normal-round branching, including in the final layer.
The conditional solver discussion does not provide an implemented key-recovery algorithm or a resource vector.

property.statement: Equation 1 composes 32 inverse-Frobenius summands per normal round into the nested expressions of Equations 4–5. With the source convention a/0=0, the algebraic identity holds at every input. The reported 14-round description has approximately 2^70 leaf terms under L(r)=32L(r-1), L(0)=1.
property.quantifier: Every AES-256 key and plaintext, with the standard dependent key expansion and the source zero-inversion convention. The count describes expression leaves; repeated leaves can share a key byte or polynomial term.
property.scope: Algebraic representation and description size. Section 4 gives conditional solver-degree observations; no attack cost or key-recovery success is established.

parameters.name: expression_rounds
parameters.meaning: Half/full expression interval with the source final-noMC counting convention.

parameters.name: expanded_term_count
parameters.meaning: Source estimate of fully unrolled nested-expression leaves. Actual terminal-round simplification is omitted.

parameters.name: generic_leaf_model
parameters.meaning: Four-by-eight branching per normal round. The estimate concerns description size.

parameters.name: source_solver_observations
parameters.reported: 7-round halves: hypothetical O(n^7); full 14 rounds: hypothetical O(n^3)
parameters.meaning: Conditional solver feasibility discussion in Section 4; solver existence and measured performance are unspecified.

validation.description: Finite checks cover 256 S-box inputs, 524288 Frobenius triples, 64 normal and 64 final-round vectors, 24 AES compositions, and 3 FIPS known-answer vectors. They verify representation components and the reported leaf-count arithmetic.
